lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before the battle, Gideon asks God for one more sign. He lays a fleece of wool on the threshing floor.

lines.speaker: gideon
lines.text: If dew is on the fleece only, and the ground is dry, then I will know You will save Israel by my hand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At dawn, Gideon wrings the fleece — a bowl of water from the wool. The ground is dry.

lines.speaker: gideon
lines.text: Let not Your anger burn against me. One more sign: let the fleece be dry, and dew be on the ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That night God does so. The fleece is dry; dew is on all the ground.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: God condescends to the weakness of one man. The fleece is not a command — it is a gift of reassurance.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The test settles. The confirmation was given, not earned. What remains is trust, not timing skill.

choices.label: March at dawn
choices.note: The story keeps its shape; Gideon carries the reassurance forward.

choices.label: Rest on the floor
choices.note: A pause does not change the outcome. It only lets the player breathe.
